title: Deuteronomy — Instructions and Commands
content:
Deuteronomy — Instructions and Commands

Instructions · All Old Testament books · Original Torah and New Testament index

16 additional passage records · 17 quoted verse units. Read Deuteronomy in Saints Translation.

This is a working instruction register organized by topic and then classification. Open a passage for its exact wording, source link and context note. Historical orders and rhetorical or poetic addresses retain their original setting; their presence here does not make them universal laws.

Read this supplement together with the existing Torah requirements. Its narrower original count is preserved. 146 selected verse units already represented by that index are cross-referenced below instead of re-entered. Other thematic overlap still requires review.

Review status: Working catalogue: the source collection covers every Old Testament book currently in Saints.Bible. Individual commands, repeated formulations, speakers and Christian application still require further review; this is not a certified exhaustive count of laws.

Topics: Faith, repentance and allegiance · Worship, prayer and holy things · Justice, truth and protection · Family, marriage and household · Historical commissions, journeys and public life

Faith, repentance and allegiance

Historical · 3 passage records

Deuteronomy 1:37

Record type: Historical direction. Source section: Command to Leave Horeb.

Deuteronomy 1:37 — And the Lord was angry with me also for your sakes, saying: You shall not enter there either.

Context and scope: A direction recorded in this narrative. Its original speaker, recipient and occasion must be retained; recording an order does not establish that God approves it or commands every believer to repeat it.

Deuteronomy 5:25

Record type: Historical direction. Source section: The Covenant at Horeb.

Deuteronomy 5:25 — And now let us not die, for this great fire will consume us; if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any more, we shall die.

Context and scope: A direction recorded in this narrative. Its original speaker, recipient and occasion must be retained; recording an order does not establish that God approves it or commands every believer to repeat it.

Record type: Historical direction. Source section: The Covenant at Horeb.

Context and scope: A direction recorded in this narrative. Its original speaker, recipient and occasion must be retained; recording an order does not establish that God approves it or commands every believer to repeat it.

Historical — rejected · 1 passage records

Deuteronomy 13:3

Record type: Reported hostile or rejected order. Source section: Idolatrous Prophets and Dreamers.

Deuteronomy 13:3 — and the sign or the wonder comes to pass, whereof he spoke unto you, saying: Let us go and serve other gods, which you have not known,

Context and scope: This order is recorded as hostile, coercive or contrary to faithful obedience in its narrative context. It is not included as a divine command to obey.
